source_control.primary: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 (June 2012)
source_control.current_law_support: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996 for sections 63-64
source_control.note: Items with legal_review_status=pending remain held from release certification until current regulations are checked.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.3 — Dipped beam

en.title: Dipped beam
en.key_point: A dipped-beam headlamp must be adjusted and maintained so that it adequately lights the road ahead.
en.explanation: The official learner manual says dipped beam must allow the driver or rider to see a person, vehicle or substantial object at least 45 metres ahead. This distance remains held for current-regulation verification before release certification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.4 — Parking lamps

en.title: Parking lamps
en.key_point: Do not drive a moving vehicle on a public road using only its parking lamps.
en.explanation: Parking lamps are not a substitute for the normal lamps required while the vehicle is being driven.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.5 — Rear lamps

en.title: Rear lamps
en.key_point: A motorcycle and a light motor vehicle used on a public road must have rear lighting that shows red to the rear.
en.explanation: Rear lamps make the vehicle visible from behind. The exact current equipment wording is being cross-checked against the operative regulations before final release certification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.6 — Stop lamp

en.title: Stop lamps
en.key_point: A light motor vehicle or motorcycle used on a public road must have rear stop lamps that show red when braking.
en.explanation: A stop lamp warns following road users that the vehicle is slowing or stopping. Detailed visibility measurements remain under current-regulation verification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.7 — Number plate lamp

en.title: Number-plate lamp
en.key_point: A motor vehicle used on a public road must have a rear number-plate lamp that illuminates the registration plate.
en.explanation: The purpose is to keep the registration plate visible at night. The manual's exact distance requirement remains under current-regulation verification.

source.locator: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996 §63 — Reckless or negligent driving

en.title: Reckless or negligent driving
en.key_point: A person may not drive a vehicle on a public road recklessly or negligently.
en.explanation: Road conditions, traffic, speed and the manner of driving all matter when deciding whether driving was reckless or negligent.

source.locator: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996 §64 — Inconsiderate driving

en.title: Inconsiderate driving
en.key_point: A person may not drive on a public road without reasonable consideration for other people using the road.
en.explanation: Safe driving includes consideration for other road users, not only avoiding a collision or breaking a speed limit.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.37 — Driving on divided public road

en.title: Driving on a divided public road
en.key_point: Use the left-hand roadway unless a traffic sign or traffic officer directs or permits you to use another roadway.
en.explanation: Where a public road is divided into separate roadways, traffic normally keeps to the left-hand roadway.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.38 — Driving on left side of roadway

en.title: Keep left on the roadway
en.key_point: Drive on the left side of the roadway and do not unnecessarily encroach into the right half.
en.explanation: Move left safely when another vehicle wants to pass and do not accelerate until it has passed.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.39 — Prohibition on driving on shoulder except in certain circumstances

en.title: Driving on the shoulder
en.key_point: Do not normally drive on the shoulder. A light vehicle may use it only in limited safe circumstances allowed by the rules.
en.explanation: The learner manual describes daytime use while being overtaken, provided it is safe and visibility is adequate. The exact conditions remain under the current-regulation verification gate.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.40 — Lane changing

en.title: Changing lanes
en.key_point: Change from one marked lane to another only when you can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic.
en.explanation: Check mirrors and blind spots, signal in good time and move only when there is a safe gap.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.42 — Direction indicators

en.title: Direction indicators
en.key_point: Use direction indicators when turning or changing lanes.
en.explanation: Indicators communicate your intended movement to other road users. Vehicle-equipment details remain subject to the current-regulation check.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.43.1 — Motorcycle retro-reflector

en.title: Motorcycle rear reflector
en.key_point: A motorcycle used on a public road must have a red retro-reflector fitted at the rear.
en.explanation: The reflector helps other road users see the motorcycle from behind in low-light conditions.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.43.2 — Light motor vehicle retro-reflectors

en.title: Light-vehicle rear reflectors
en.key_point: A light motor vehicle must have red retro-reflectors at the rear.
en.explanation: The learner manual specifies one on each side. The exact current equipment wording is being checked against operative regulations.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.45 — Overtaking/passing, limited left-passing exceptions

en.title: Passing on the left
en.key_point: Overtaking is normally on the right. Passing on the left is allowed only in specific safe situations permitted by the rules.
en.explanation: Do not treat the left side as a general overtaking lane. The detailed exceptions remain tied to the official rule set and current-regulation check.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.50 — Duties relating to motorcycles

en.title: Motorcycle rider control
en.key_point: Ride so that you maintain complete control of the motorcycle and a clear view of the road and traffic.
en.explanation: Baggage must be carried so that it does not obstruct your view or prevent proper control.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.50 — Rider/passenger must not take hold of another moving vehicle

en.title: Do not hold onto another moving vehicle
en.key_point: A motorcycle rider or passenger must not take hold of another vehicle that is moving.
en.explanation: The motorcycle must be controlled independently and safely at all times.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.50 — Motorcycles in single file, subject to overtaking rule

en.title: Motorcycles travelling together
en.key_point: Motorcycles travelling in the same lane should ride in single file, except as allowed while overtaking.
en.explanation: The rule reduces conflict between motorcycles sharing the same lane and other road users.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.51 — Sidecar attachment

en.title: Motorcycle sidecar
en.key_point: A sidecar used on a public road must be attached on the correct side of the motorcycle.
en.explanation: The learner manual specifies the left side and contains an engine-capacity condition. Those equipment details remain under current-regulation verification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.54 — Vehicle left/abandoned

en.title: Leaving a vehicle on a public road
en.key_point: Do not leave a vehicle standing indefinitely on a public road.
en.explanation: The learner manual sets different time periods inside and outside urban areas. Those exact periods remain under the current-regulation verification gate before release certification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.55 — Damage to public roads

en.title: Do not damage the road
en.key_point: Do not operate or move a vehicle in a way that damages the roadway.
en.explanation: The manual also prohibits deliberately dragging or spinning wheels on the road except in an emergency.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.56 — Freeways: prohibited vehicles/users

en.title: Who may use a freeway
en.key_point: Not every road user or vehicle is allowed on a freeway.
en.explanation: The official learner manual excludes several slow or unsuitable road users and vehicle types. Exact category thresholds remain under current-regulation verification.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.56 — Freeway stopping, pedestrians/animals and merging

en.title: Freeway behaviour
en.key_point: Do not stop on a freeway except where the rules allow it, and remain alert to vehicles merging from on-ramps.
en.explanation: The manual also restricts pedestrians and animals on freeways and requires drivers to allow a vehicle ahead to merge safely from an on-ramp.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.8 — Number plates

en.title: Number plates
en.key_point: Number plates must be fitted in the prescribed positions and must be clearly legible and visible.
en.explanation: The learner manual places a plate at the rear of a motorcycle, motor tricycle or trailer, and at both the front and rear of other motor vehicles.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.9 — Fog lamps

en.title: Fog lamps
en.key_point: Fog lamps should be used only when visibility is poor because of conditions such as fog, mist, dust, smoke or snow.
en.explanation: Do not use fog lamps as ordinary driving lights in clear conditions.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.10 — Spot lamp

en.title: Spot lamps
en.key_point: An adjustable spot lamp is not for ordinary unrestricted road use.
en.explanation: The learner manual limits adjustable spot-lamp use to specified official, emergency, professional and essential-service purposes.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.11 — Driving view unobstructed / rear-view mirrors

en.title: Clear driving view and mirrors
en.key_point: The driver or rider must have a clear view ahead and to both sides and must be able to see traffic behind using suitable mirrors.
en.explanation: For light vehicles, the learner manual explains the required exterior/interior mirror arrangement and the additional exterior mirror needed when an interior mirror cannot give a clear rear view.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.12.1 — Motorcycle steering gear

en.title: Motorcycle steering gear
en.key_point: Motorcycle steering gear must allow safe and efficient steering and the handlebars must comply with the official dimensions.
en.explanation: The learner manual states handlebar widths of 600–800 mm for motorcycles of 200 cc or more, and 500–800 mm below 200 cc, with limits on handgrip height relative to the seat.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.12.2 — Light motor vehicle steering gear

en.title: Light-vehicle steering gear
en.key_point: All steering parts must be maintained so that the vehicle can be steered safely and efficiently.
en.explanation: A vehicle with defective steering must not be used on a public road.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.13 — Turning radius

en.title: Turning radius
en.key_point: The learner manual states that a motor vehicle used on a public road may not have a turning radius exceeding 13.1 metres.
en.explanation: This is part of the published vehicle-roadworthiness study material.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.14.1 — Motorcycle brakes

en.title: Motorcycle braking systems
en.key_point: A motorcycle must have two independent braking systems: one acting on the front wheel and one on the rear wheel or wheels.
en.explanation: Both braking systems must be in proper working order.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.19 — Windscreen

en.title: Windscreen
en.key_point: The windscreen must provide enough visibility for safe driving and must be made of safety glass.
en.explanation: The learner manual also states a minimum visible-light transmittance of 70 percent through the windscreen.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.20 — Windscreen wipers

en.title: Windscreen wipers
en.key_point: A vehicle with a windscreen must have at least one effective windscreen wiper.
en.explanation: The wiper must clear the outside of the windscreen directly in front of the driver continuously and adequately.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.21 — Exhaust silencers / exhaust pipes

en.title: Exhaust system
en.key_point: A motor vehicle must have an effective exhaust silencer and must not emit exhaust in a way that creates danger, nuisance or obstructed visibility.
en.explanation: The exhaust system must also be positioned and maintained so that fumes do not leak into the driver or passenger area.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.22 — Fuel tank, electrical wiring and battery

en.title: Fuel system, wiring and battery
en.key_point: Fuel-system parts, electrical wiring and the battery must be safely installed, maintained and not create a source of danger.
en.explanation: The fuel tank must also have an effective cap.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.23 — Engine

en.title: Engine safety
en.key_point: A light motor vehicle must have its engine covered so that it is not a source of danger.
en.explanation: This forms part of the official learner roadworthiness material.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.24 — Emergency warning signs (triangles)

en.title: Emergency warning triangle
en.key_point: Certain goods vehicles, minibuses, buses and heavy vehicles must carry an emergency warning triangle; ordinary motor cars and motorcycles are excluded in the learner manual.
en.explanation: When required for a stationary vehicle, the manual places the triangle at least 45 metres away in the direction from which traffic approaches, with the reflective side facing approaching traffic.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.25 — Excessive noise

en.title: Excessive vehicle noise
en.key_point: Do not operate a vehicle on a public road in a way that causes excessive noise.
en.explanation: This rule applies to both riders and drivers.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.26 — Speedometers

en.title: Speedometer
en.key_point: A motor vehicle designed for or capable of 60 km/h or more must have a speedometer in good working order.
en.explanation: The speedometer allows the driver or rider to monitor road speed.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.28 — Passenger vehicles conveying persons for reward

en.title: Passenger vehicles for reward
en.key_point: The learner manual states a 100 km/h maximum for a bus or minibus conveying passengers for reward.
en.explanation: This is a vehicle-class rule and does not replace a lower posted speed limit.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.30 — Overall length of vehicles

en.title: Overall vehicle length
en.key_point: Vehicle length is legally limited by vehicle type.
en.explanation: For the ordinary 'other vehicle' category in the learner manual, overall length may not exceed 12.5 metres. Longer limits apply to specified trailers, articulated vehicles, bus-trains and vehicle combinations.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.31 — Overall height of vehicle

en.title: Overall vehicle height
en.key_point: For vehicles other than a double-deck bus, the learner manual states a maximum overall height of 4.3 metres including the load.
en.explanation: A double-deck bus has a separate published limit.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.32 — Overall width of vehicles

en.title: Overall vehicle width
en.key_point: For the ordinary 'other vehicle' category, the learner manual states a maximum overall width of 2.5 metres.
en.explanation: Specified buses and large goods vehicles have a separate 2.6-metre rule.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.33 — Conveyance of goods

en.title: Loads on a light vehicle
en.key_point: Loads must be secure, must not touch the road or block the driver's view, and must stay within the official load limits.
en.explanation: The learner manual also limits the height of ordinary goods carried on a motor-car roof to half the vehicle's height, with an exception for bicycles carried on the roof.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.34 — Persons carried on goods vehicle

en.title: Persons on a goods vehicle
en.key_point: If people are carried on a goods vehicle, the carrying area must have protective enclosure of the height stated in the learner manual.
en.explanation: The manual states at least 350 mm above a seated person’s surface or 900 mm above a standing surface, and says passengers may not ride in a caravan.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.35 — Motorcycle projections / overhang

en.title: Motorcycle load projections
en.key_point: Goods on a motorcycle or sidecar must stay within the official projection limits.
en.explanation: The learner manual states no more than 600 mm in front of the front axle, 900 mm behind the rear axle, 450 mm beyond either side of the motorcycle wheels, and 300 mm beyond the outside of a sidecar wheel.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.35 — Light vehicle projections / overhang

en.title: Light-vehicle load projections
en.key_point: A load on an ordinary light vehicle must stay within the official side, front and rear projection limits.
en.explanation: The learner manual gives 1.25 m from the centre line to either side, 300 mm beyond the front and 1.8 m beyond the rear, with a separate 150 mm limit for brackets beyond the widest part.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.36 — Warning flags / reflectors

en.title: Marking a projecting load
en.key_point: A load projecting more than the published limits must be marked so other road users can see it.
en.explanation: The learner manual requires a red 300 mm × 300 mm flag by day where a load projects more than 150 mm to the side or 300 mm to the rear, and white front/red rear reflectors at night or in poor visibility.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.46 — Intersections / traffic-circle right of way

en.title: Intersections and right of way
en.key_point: At an uncontrolled traffic circle or similar junction, yield to traffic approaching from the right unless a traffic officer or sign gives a different instruction.
en.explanation: Always obey traffic officers and traffic signs when they control the intersection.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.47 — Parking

en.title: Parking restrictions
en.key_point: Do not park where a sign prohibits it, where you block access or visibility, or within the official distances and restricted places listed in the learner manual.
en.explanation: Examples include within 1.5 m of a fire hydrant, within 9 m before a pedestrian crossing, within 5 m of an intersection, on a traffic island or pedestrian area, or where the road is too narrow.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.48 — Stopping

en.title: Stopping restrictions
en.key_point: Do not stop on the roadway where stopping would obstruct or endanger other traffic, unless stopping is necessary for safety, required by an officer or beyond your control.
en.explanation: Stopping restrictions are stricter than ordinary parking rules because even a short stop can create a hazard.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.49 — General duties of driver/rider

en.title: General duties of a driver or rider
en.key_point: Maintain control, keep a safe following distance, reverse only when safe and avoid actions that obstruct your view or control.
en.explanation: These general duties apply even where no separate sign is present.

source.locator: NaTIS Rules of the Road v1.01 §6.65 — Driving while impaired

en.title: Never drive while impaired
en.key_point: Do not drive or ride when alcohol, medication or another substance makes you unsafe to control the vehicle.
en.explanation: The safest learner rule is simple: impairment and driving do not mix. The app does not teach learners to calculate how much of an intoxicating substance they could use before driving.
